explanations.text:
How human works — seven things you can ask for, told as flows.
On the left, who acts: you, claude, the tool, the disk.


flow 1 · decompile — the code exists, the words come after

  you      ask for a file: /decompile src/app.py
  claude   reads the file and picks the shape from the kind of file,
           by [the decompile skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/decompile/SKILL.md) and
           [the shape catalog](compiler/cli/human/shapes/README.md): one run takes the rail,
           a set of functions the sections, a dispatcher the desk, a rulebook the dialogue.
  claude   writes the telling for [a reader who does not read code](compiler/cli/human/skills/decompile/SKILL.md:e1:explain),
           with pins on the words that name a thing. Every other word is free.
  claude   shows the text and stops — even when your message sounded like approval.
  you      say the word: map it.
  claude   pipes the exact text into [human map](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:cmd_map).
  tool     gates the entry, no claude call: [every pin points at a real thing](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:build_anchors),
           no two pins share their words, [no circle](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:check_cycle),
           and each block pin gets [its exact lines](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:block_spans).
           A refusal is the gate speaking: claude reads it, fixes the text, runs again.
  disk     one entry appended to human/explanation_<path>.json, never one changed.
  claude   [reports](compiler/cli/human/skills/decompile/SKILL.md:e1:report): the entry, its pins, the coverage,
           the warnings of [human show](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:cmd_show) — and offers the next telling:
           a zoom on one block, a plainer layer over the whole, or [the project itself](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:cmd_map_project),
           whose pins reach the files and the entries of their maps.


flow 2 · compile — your words come first, the code after

  you      give an abstraction: /human an http server that returns hello world
  claude   follows [the human skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md): [the run](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:e1:the run)
           keeps your words verbatim in abstraction.txt — no spelling fixed, no word trimmed.
  claude   writes the code files, no comments. The gate is static like a compiler's: the file must parse.
  tool     [human init](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the register) registers the project: [sweeps the tree](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the sweep)
           through [the ignore sieve](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the sieve), writes the file list into human/human.json,
           copies the reader in, and starts the empty project map.
  claude   maps the detailed telling of each file — entry 1, a catalog shape, pins into the blocks.
  claude   maps your words on top: pins inserted, the rest untouched, through [the verbatim gate](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the guard),
           which strips the pins out and compares the rest against abstraction.txt character for character.
           A changed word is a refusal. Pins go in; your words never change.
  claude   reports and serves. Afterwards you correct with retext, undo, sync — the commands of flow 1.


flow 3 · read

  you      start the reader from anywhere in the project: human serve
  tool     [climbs to the folder that holds human/human.json](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:find_root) and [serves it](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the shelf),
           printing the localhost line and [the tailnet line](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:tailnet address).
  tool     answers human.json with [a live file list](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:rebuilt) — a fresh sweep on every ask,
           so a deleted file leaves the tree and a new one appears, no init, no restart.
  you      open [the reader](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html): human.json opens first, project.json stands under it;
           a file shows [every entry as one folded header](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:render), the most detailed first;
           a click on a pin [jumps to its entry](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:jump), and a pin into another file
           [switches file](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:crossJump) — a project pin lands on the entry and lights the anchor.


flow 4 · sync — the code changed

  you      change the code, then: human sync src/app.py
  tool     [a deterministic pass](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:cmd_sync), no claude: [maps every old line to its new line](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the line map),
           [re-resolves every pin and every span](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the re-resolving). Lines that only moved end here.
  tool     finds the entries the change touches: lines changed, a pin broken, new lines inside the block.
  tool     writes the letter to claude: the file and its absolute path — read the whole file —, the diff,
           [the project files it imports](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the line about the neighbours), the blocks, the entries to mend, the rules:
           keep the untouched lines, keep every anchor, add a sentence for each behaviour the change added.
  claude   [answers with the mended texts](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:ask_claude), run at the project root.
  tool     [gates the answer on a copy](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the rebuild), up to --tries times: every block exists,
           every anchor kept, every needed word alive. Four failures leave the map untouched.
  disk     the map saved; the entries that point into a mended one marked stale — in the file's map,
           and in the project map when a project entry pins the mended one.
           A warning when [new lines landed inside an entry](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the pieces the new lines fall in) and no word changed.
  you      for the whole project: human sync project. The old state is git HEAD; the tool asks git for
           [the files that changed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:changed_files), re-resolves the file, block, and entry pins,
           and [sends one letter](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:cmd_sync) for the entries that pin a changed file.


flow 5 · carry down — a parent telling changed

  disk     entry 1 changed — by a sync or a retext — and entry 2 points into it,
           so [entry 2 is marked stale](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:mark_children) with a copy of the old text.
  you      ask for the repair: human sync src/app.py --stale 2
  tool     writes the second letter: the old text of the parent, the new text, the diff, the dependent's text,
           the rules: mend the words that went wrong, keep every anchor and [every word another entry needs](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:needed_words),
           carry a new fact down at the dependent's own level, pinned at the parent's new anchor.
  claude   answers with the mended dependent — words only, never code.
  tool     [gates and saves](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:repair_stale); the dependents of entry 2 are marked stale in turn.
           A parent's child can be a parent: the next layer waits for your next word, one layer at a time.
           A project entry made stale by a file's entry is repaired the same way,
           with the parent read from that file's map: [human sync project --stale](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:repair_stale).


flow 6 · train — the catalog learns from real picks

  you      open a session: human train --open. [Rows without a pick carry over](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:carry).
  claude   on the next /decompile or sync, writes three versions per file instead of one:
           best — the catalog shape, with --shape; refinement — for a sync row, the map's own text,
           filled by the tool; free — no shape rule. [Each version goes in with its own call](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:cmd_add),
           passes the same pin gates as a map, and a rewrite keeps its earlier text in the history.
  tool     serves [the feed](compiler/cli/human/reader/feed.html): the session list and the fresh map come as JSON;
           [a pick lands in the open session](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:pick) over POST, no restart.
  you      swipe and pick — sideways for the versions, down for the next file — and leave a comment if you want.
  you      close: human train --close.
  tool     [applies each pick](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:apply_row) as a retext of the entry or a new map, then [marks the session finished](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:cmd_close).
           The maps never change before the close.
  disk     human/training/<session>.json: the rows, the three versions with their shape and history,
           the pick, the comment, and a copy of the code — or, for the project, [of every file](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:snapshot).


flow 7 · shapes — how the catalog changes

  claude   reads the finished sessions: which slot won, which shape it wore, what the comment said.
  claude   tells you what it learned and the fix it would make, by [the shapes skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/shapes/SKILL.md):
           [the smallest change that would have produced the ideal](compiler/cli/human/skills/shapes/SKILL.md:e1:the comparison) —
           a new shape, a rule added or changed, or the example changed.
  you      [validate, or not](compiler/cli/human/skills/shapes/SKILL.md:e1:the validation). Without the word, the catalog does not change.
  claude   edits shapes/<shape>.md, bumps the version, reinstalls, and redeploys with [human skills](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the giver).
           The next /decompile reads the new rule.
